nodes.name: Unit ball
nodes.statement: The unit ball S in d dimensions is the set of all points x in R^d with |x| <= 1.

nodes.name: Spherical Gaussian
nodes.statement: The d-dimensional spherical Gaussian with zero mean and variance sigma^2 in each coordinate has density p(x) = (1/(2*pi)^{d/2} * sigma^d) * exp(-|x|^2 / (2*sigma^2)).

nodes.name: Random projection
nodes.statement: The random projection f: R^d -> R^k is defined as f(v) = (u_1.v, u_2.v, ..., u_k.v) where u_1, ..., u_k are random Gaussian vectors in R^d with unit-variance coordinates.

nodes.name: Markov's inequality
nodes.statement: For a nonneg. random variable x and a > 0: Prob(x >= a) <= E(x)/a.
assumptions: x is a nonnegative random variable

nodes.statement: Split E(x) = integral from 0 to a + integral from a to infinity. The second part is >= a * Prob(x >= a).
nodes.proof_strategy: direct computation, splitting integral at a

nodes.statement: Prob(x >= b*E(x)) <= 1/b for nonneg. x and b > 0.
assumptions: x is a nonnegative random variable

nodes.name: Chebyshev's inequality
nodes.statement: For any random variable x with finite variance and c > 0: Prob(|x - E(x)| >= c) <= Var(x)/c^2.
assumptions: x is a random variable with finite variance

nodes.statement: Apply Markov's inequality to y = |x - E(x)|^2 with threshold c^2. Since E(y) = Var(x), the result follows.

nodes.name: Law of Large Numbers
nodes.statement: For n independent samples of x, the sample mean concentrates: Prob(|avg - E(x)| >= eps) <= Var(x)/(n*eps^2).
assumptions: x_1, ..., x_n are n independent samples of random variable x

nodes.statement: Apply Chebyshev to the sample mean. Var of the average = Var(x)/n by independence and scaling.

nodes.name: Master Tail Bounds Theorem
nodes.statement: Under bounded moment conditions on independent zero-mean variables, the sum x = x_1+...+x_n has sub-Gaussian tail: Prob(|x| >= a) <= 3*exp(-a^2/(12*n*sigma^2)).
assumptions: x_i are mutually independent with zero mean and Var(x_i) <= sigma^2

nodes.name: Volume and surface area of unit ball
nodes.statement: A(d) = 2*pi^(d/2)/Gamma(d/2) and V(d) = 2*pi^(d/2)/(d*Gamma(d/2)). The volume V(d) -> 0 as d -> infinity.
Evaluate the Gaussian integral I(d) in Cartesian coords (gives pi^(d/2)) and polar coords (gives A(d)*Gamma(d/2)/2). Equate to solve for A(d).
nodes.proof_strategy: compute Gaussian integral in two coordinate systems

nodes.name: Volume near the equator
nodes.statement: For c>=1, d>=3: at least 1-(2/c)*exp(-c^2/2) fraction of the unit ball volume has |x_1| <= c/sqrt(d-1). Most volume is near any equator.
conclusions: At least 1 - (2/c)*exp(-c^2/2) fraction of volume has |x_1| <= c/sqrt(d-1)

nodes.statement: Upper-bound the volume above the slice using 1-x <= e^{-x} and extending integral to infinity. Lower-bound the hemisphere volume by an inscribed cylinder. Take the ratio.
nodes.proof_strategy: volume ratio bound via integral estimates

nodes.name: Near-orthogonality of random points
nodes.statement: n random points from the d-dim unit ball are all near unit length and pairwise nearly orthogonal (dot product O(sqrt(ln n)/sqrt(d))) with prob 1-O(1/n).
assumptions: n points drawn uniformly from d-dimensional unit ball
conclusions: |x_i . x_j| <= sqrt(6*ln(n))/sqrt(d-1) for all i != j (w.h.p.)

nodes.statement: Part 1: each |x_i| is near 1 by volume concentration; union bound over n. Part 2: fix x_i as north pole, x_j's projection is small by Thm 2.7; union bound over n choose 2 pairs.

nodes.name: Gaussian Annulus Theorem
nodes.statement: A d-dim unit-variance Gaussian concentrates in a thin annulus: all but 3*exp(-c*beta^2) of the mass lies within sqrt(d) +/- beta of the origin.
assumptions: d-dimensional spherical Gaussian with unit variance
conclusions: All but 3*exp(-c*beta^2) of mass lies in annulus sqrt(d)-beta <= |x| <= sqrt(d)+beta

nodes.statement: Write |x|^2 - d = sum(x_i^2 - 1), a sum of zero-mean independent variables. Bound moments, rescale, apply Master Tail Bounds Theorem.
nodes.proof_strategy: change of variables + Master Tail Bounds (Thm 2.5)

nodes.name: Random Projection Theorem
nodes.statement: Projecting v onto k random Gaussian directions preserves length: ||f(v)| - sqrt(k)*|v|| < eps*sqrt(k)*|v| with prob >= 1 - 3*exp(-c*k*eps^2).
assumptions: v is a fixed vector in R^d
f is a random Gaussian projection to R^k

nodes.statement: WLOG |v|=1. Each u_i.v is Gaussian(0,1), so f(v) is a k-dim spherical Gaussian. Apply Gaussian Annulus Theorem with d=k.

nodes.name: Johnson-Lindenstrauss Lemma
nodes.statement: Random projection to k = O(ln(n)/eps^2) dimensions preserves ALL pairwise distances up to (1+/-eps) with high probability.
Apply Random Projection Theorem to each difference v_i - v_j. Per-pair failure prob <= 3/n^3. Union bound over C(n,2) < n^2/2 pairs.

nodes.name: MLE mean is the centroid
nodes.statement: The sum of squared distances from n points to a center mu is minimized when mu is the centroid (1/n)*sum(x_i).
assumptions: x_1, ..., x_n are n points in R^d
conclusions: sum(|x_i - mu|^2) is minimized at mu = (1/n)*sum(x_i)

nodes.statement: Set gradient of sum(|x_i - mu|^2) to zero: -2*sum(x_i - mu) = 0, solve for mu.

nodes.name: MLE spherical Gaussian
nodes.statement: The MLE spherical Gaussian has center = sample mean and sigma = sample standard deviation.
assumptions: x_1, ..., x_n sampled from a spherical Gaussian in R^d
conclusions: MLE sigma = sample std dev from the true mean

nodes.name: Generating random points from a ball
nodes.statement: Generate x with each coordinate ~ N(0,1). Normalize to x/|x| (uniform on sphere). Scale by rho with density d*r^{d-1} on [0,1]. Result y = rho*x/|x| is uniform in the ball.

nodes.name: Separating two Gaussians
nodes.statement: Compute all pairwise distances. The cluster with smallest pairwise distances comes from one Gaussian; remove and the rest form the second. Requires center separation Omega(d^{1/4}).

edges.note: proof applies Markov to squared deviation
proof applies Chebyshev to sample mean
Master Tail Bounds extends Markov's approach
